This goes through the New-Project Entry. Nothing is built: the package is a greeting `main()` and two smoke tests, and there is no spec. The outcomes below are candidates I drew from your brief, `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`. The three research files supplied only facts and costs. Please confirm, cut or reword any outcome; I haven't ranked them.

**Candidate outcomes** (all from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`)

| # | Outcome | Track | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision magnitude over time (mean absolute revision, dispersion, tails) for each of the four stages, total nonfarm, SA and NSA | A | Small data: monthly series × a few hundred vintages, megabytes. The ALFRED API allows about 120 requests/min. NSA vintage depth is unconfirmed. |
| O2 | O1 extended to the NAICS supersectors | A | Same order as O1. Supersector vintage coverage in ALFRED is unconfirmed and may need archived releases. |
| O3 | Split of SA one- and two-month revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, by vintage | A | Low compute once O1's vintages exist. Factors come from the SA/NSA ratio per vintage. All three research files call this unstudied over the long run. |
| O4 | Benchmark and wedge-back record: preliminary and final March benchmark revisions per year, with the wedge spread over the intervening months | A | Mostly your time: about 20–40 annual benchmark articles to transcribe. Only running the work can tell how many are machine-readable. |
| O5 | How much collection interval and first-closing rate move one-month revision dispersion | B | The calendar part can be computed cheaply. The start date of the published collection-rate series is unconfirmed. |
| O6 | Annual covariate set: real BLS appropriations, FTE, CES sample size, shutdowns, CRs and sequestration | B | Your time, likely tens of hours. Basis: about 35 fiscal years of budget justifications, which are thinner and less often online before the mid-1990s. |
| O7 | Bayesian multi-vintage state-space model of revision scale (latent path, stage-specific news and noise, SV with covariates in log-scale, Student-t, benchmark as an irregular observation), total nonfarm | B | Fit time is unknown; the core stage would measure it. It is about 500 months × 4 stages, with the latent state marginalized by Kalman filtering. |
| O8 | Partial pooling of driver effects across supersectors | B | A multiple of O7's fit cost; measured after O7 runs. |
| O9 | Validation: LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks, revision-targeted predictive checks | B | Pseudo-real-time means one refit per cutoff, a multiple of O7's cost. |

**Tracks**
- **A: Descriptive revision history**, which I propose as a known progression. It answers *what happened* to revision scale, stage by stage. That result can be used or published on its own.
- **B: Drivers of revision scale**, which I propose as research, because the method and the identifiability of the capacity covariates are open.

I split them because joining them would make O1's history wait on the state-space and SV machinery, while B uses A's vintage panel and not the reverse. If you would rather treat A as research too, say so.

**Choices already made**
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), with uv.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if a custom kernel is warranted, ArviZ, and Polars for the vintage panel. These come from your brief's implementation notes.
- One flag: I haven't confirmed that JAX ships wheels for Python 3.14. That needs a cheap read-only check before Track B starts.

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, which gives `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

**Optional probe:** list the vintage dates for PAYEMS and PAYNSA in ALFRED. This would firm up the coverage notes for O1–O3. I'll run it only if you say yes.

**My request:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds, the outcome list and the name.
